title: [YouPass Collect] - Employment by Gender and Sector: 1990–2010
prompt: The table beneath shows the level of people specialists in various kinds of enterprises in 1990, 2000, and 2010. Sum up the data by choosing and writing about the primary capacities and make correlations where fitting.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table compares the percentages of male and female employees working in four different sectors, namely retail, health, manufacturing, and tourism, over a 20-year period from 1990 to 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, male employment showed mixed trends, with manufacturing declining most dramatically, while female figures rose across all sectors except this industry. Additionally, tourism remained the most popular sector for female workers throughout the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding male employees, in 1990, manufacturing was the leading sector at 30%, more than double that of retail and tourism, which both stood at 13%, while health recorded the lowest proportion at just 7%. Over the following two decades, the figure for manufacturing experienced a dramatic fall, dropping to 15% in 2000 before reaching only 10% by 2010. Meanwhile, the percentage for tourism fell slightly to 10% in 2000 and remained at this level by 2010, while retail was unchanged at 13% throughout. The health sector, on the other hand, held steady at 7% in 2000 before rising marginally to 9% at the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for female workers, tourism dominated with 23% in 1990, significantly higher than health at 9%, while retail and manufacturing were equal at 7%. This figure continued its upward trend, rising to 25% in 2000 before reaching 27% by 2010. Similarly, the proportion of women in health increased steadily from 11% to 15% over the same period. Retail also witnessed modest growth to 8% and 9% in 2000 and 2010, respectively, whereas manufacturing peaked at 8% in 2000 then dropped sharply to just 3%.
